title: Understanding the Savannah Guthrie Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Curious about the Savannah Guthrie salary? Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay using Australian award rates, tax, and super. Fair Work and ATO figures explained.
salarySummary: Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming a standard 38-hour week, with super paid on top and tax applied from the 2026–27 resident scale.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time employee on 38 hours per week, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. Super is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates are minimum wages set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations, and they are generally higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the Children's Services Award and Pharmacy Award have recently increased due to gender-based undervaluation reviews. Always check the relevant award for your correct minimum rate.

faqs.q: Does the Savannah Guthrie salary figure come from official Australian sources?
faqs.a: No, the search results from the Fair Work Commission and Fair Work Ombudsman do not contain any data on Savannah Guthrie's salary. Those sources provide authoritative Australian wage information, such as modern award rates and the National Minimum Wage. Any figure for a US television host like Savannah Guthrie would come from overseas media, not Australian government agencies. Use our conversion tool to estimate annual pay from any hourly rate you input.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you’ve ever searched for the **Savannah Guthrie salary**, you’ve probably seen a wide range of figures from entertainment news. But when it comes to Australian pay, the rules are clear and set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission. Whether you’re an employee on an award, a casual worker, or comparing a salary offer, understanding how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay is essential. This guide walks you through the formula, the key rates, and what to expect for tax and super.

## The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

Australia’s minimum pay floor is the **National Minimum Wage**. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. If you’re a casual employee, you also get a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

However, most employees are covered by a **modern award** that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database, which contains the calculated minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each award. For example, award wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026, and some awards like the Children’s Services Award and Pharmacy Award have had additional increases from gender-based undervaluation reviews.

So when you hear a figure like the **Savannah Guthrie salary**, remember that it’s not based on Australian award rates. Our system ensures that every employee receives at least the minimum set by their award or the National Minimum Wage, whichever is higher.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual

The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a standard full-time week of **38 hours**. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. For example:

- National Minimum Wage full-time: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44 per year (before tax and super).
- Casual minimum: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 per year.

To find your **fortnightly pay**, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage, that’s $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 before tax.

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly amounts. Remember: never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool adds it for you.

## The Role of Superannuation and Tax

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross is $52,245, your employer must contribute an extra $6,269.40 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay – it’s an additional benefit.

**Income tax** for 2026–27 residents is:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (using 2025–26 thresholds for singles as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,245), the estimated tax plus Medicare would be around $7,500–$8,000, leaving a take-home pay of roughly $44,000–$45,000 per year.

For more detail on tax and super, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) pages.

## Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) is the simplest way to see your annual pay. Just type your base hourly rate (e.g., $30.00) and check the casual loading box if applicable. The tool does the rest: 38-hour week × 52 weeks, plus super and tax estimates. It’s ideal for comparing a salary offer against an hourly rate, or for checking that your pay meets the award minimum.

If you’re covered by an award, you can find your exact classification rate in the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. The [reference tables](/data) also list common rates for quick lookup.

## Conclusion

Whether you’re chasing the **Savannah Guthrie salary** out of curiosity or calculating your own earnings, the principles are the same: hourly rate × hours × 52. But in Australia, your minimum pay is protected by the Fair Work system. Always check the relevant award or the National Minimum Wage, and remember that super is extra and tax is progressive. Use our timesheet to get an instant estimate, and consult official sources for your specific situation.
